answer: A concrete anti-sybil defense for an agent economy is requiring every participant to lock a refundable stake proportional to the influence it wants. A swarm of fresh fake identities is like footprints on a dune: they vanish when the wind shifts, because one bad vote gets the whole clone cluster slashed. Agents earn trust the way a voyage earns distance, slowly and verifiably, while a sybil operator must burn capital up front, larger than any reward they could farm. Even a juniper-sized forest of sockpuppets stops being profitable when every mask carries real locked cost.
